title: Input to the `system.capabilities` MCP tool
description:
What a caller may send to `system.capabilities`: nothing. SEC-12 validates every call against this file before it reaches application code, in the MCP server middleware (ADR-0031 decision 2).

**No `$ref` to `tool-context.schema.json`, and that is derived rather than assumed.** This tool reports what the *daemon* can do — which optional stores were built, which protocol version it speaks — and its handler takes no arguments, so referencing a context that *requires* `projectId` would publish a contract refusing every call this build serves. ADR-0031 decision 1 fixes the composition for project-scoped tools; which tools those are is decided by the handlers.

**The closure is still `unevaluatedProperties: false`**, uniformly with the tools that do compose: with no `properties` declared and no `allOf` branch to evaluate, every key a caller sends is unevaluated and therefore refused. One keyword across the set is what lets a single test hold the closure claim over all of them.

A capability report that varied with an argument would be a different kind of object than this one: taking no input is what makes the answer a property of the installation rather than of the question.
